programs.title: Pad A Girl Child
programs.description:
Impact in action! 

As part of our Pad A Girl intervention in Langtang North, OCHAWORTHLACDI in partnership with bambam soya oil distributed 350 sanitary pads to girls at Government Secondary School (GSS) Langtang.

Every pad distributed represents more than menstrual hygiene ... it represents dignity, confidence, and a girl’s right to stay in school without interruption.

Together, we are breaking stigma, fighting period poverty, and creating a future where no girl is held back by her period.

Changing lives, one girl at a time !!!❤️

Our Pad A Girl intervention continued at Government Secondary School (GSS) Shishiri, Langtang North, where girls received sanitary pads and menstrual health education.

In collaboration with @bambamsoyaoil , we are helping girls manage their periods with dignity, stay in school, and pursue their dreams without interruption.

Together, we’re breaking stigma, ending period poverty, and creating a future where every girl has the support she needs to thrive.

programs.title: World Cancer Day Walk
programs.description:
OWLACDI and the Plateau Health Ministry are really pushing for cancer awareness and early detection in Plateau State. The message is clear: cancer isn’t a death sentence if caught early and treated properly.

Some key takeaways:
- *United by Unique*: Emphasizing personalized care and collective action against cancer.
- *Awareness and Screening*: Many still lack basic knowledge about cancer; promoting early detection and screenings is crucial.
- *Government Support*: Need for prioritized cancer research, treatment, and affordable care, especially for vulnerable groups.
- *Prevention*: Vaccination, healthy lifestyles, and avoiding risk factors can reduce cancer risk.

The Plateau State Government is strengthening cancer prevention and control through public awareness, screenings, and collaborations. What’s your take on how communities can support cancer awareness?
